If the area of rectangle ABCD is 8, what is the value of $a$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} According to the problem, the area of rectangle ABCD is $a+6=8$,

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: the image shows a rectangle ABCD above the x-axis, with AB horizontal, AD and BC vertical, D and C on the x-axis, and the y-axis passing between D and C. Point A is on the left inverse-proportion branch and point B is on the right branch. Let the common height of A and B be y=t because AB is parallel to the x-axis. From the text, A lies on y=-a/x, so t=-a/x_A and hence x_A=-a/t. B lies on y=6/x, so t=6/x_B and hence x_B=6/t. The rectangle height is t and its width is x_B-x_A=6/t-(-a/t)=(a+6)/t. Therefore its area is t·(a+6)/t=a+6. Use the given area 8 to solve a+6=8, giving a=2.
